message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (about 0.1 atm), pure water freezes at roughly **–2 °C**.  
This is slightly below the standard 0 °C freezing point at 1 atm because the lower pressure reduces the temperature at which the solid and liquid phases are in equilibrium.
